title: Preterite and imperfect: telling Perón's story

sections.content: You know the *indefinido* and the *imperfecto* from A2 Unit 22 (the preterite vs the imperfect). Use the preterite for the events that move the story forward (*marcharon*, *habló*) and the imperfect for the background: what things were like, what was going on, a person's age. Perón's story needs both.

items.spanish: Perón era coronel cuando los militares tomaron el poder en 1943.
items.english: Perón was a colonel when the military took power in 1943.

items.spanish: Los obreros trabajaban mucho y tenían pocos derechos.
items.english: The workers worked a lot and had few rights.

items.spanish: Mientras la multitud esperaba en la plaza, Perón habló desde un balcón.
items.english: While the crowd was waiting in the square, Perón spoke from a balcony.

items.spanish: Eva Perón murió en 1952, cuando tenía 33 años.
items.english: Eva Perón died in 1952, when she was 33.

sections.content: Ask yourself: is this a step in the story (preterite) or the scene around it (imperfect)? A date or a single moment (*en 1952*, *el 17 de octubre*) usually goes with the preterite; *mientras* + a long background action goes with the imperfect.
